50.0.s.en: 1. The works of Simon son of Onias

50.0.0.en: 1 Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple. 2 And by him was founded the double height, the high fortification of the wall about the temple. 3 In his days the wells of waters were dug, and the cistern, like the sea, reached its full measure of overflowing. 4 He took thought for his people that they should not perish, and fortified the city that it should not be taken.

50.1.0.en: Simon the son of Onias, the high priest, the leader of his brethren and the glory of his people[4], was the one who repaired the house in his life, and fortified the temple in his days [1].

50.1.1.en: He also laid the foundation of the wall of double height, and of the strong wall surrounding the temple [2].

50.1.2.en: In his days a reservoir of waters was dug, a cistern like the sea in its circuit (or borders) [3].

50.2.0.en: He dug the great basin in the midst of the temple to supply the needs of the sacrifices, the purification and the washing. In the days of Pontius Pilate this huge cistern was still standing; water was brought to it from outside Jerusalem, and its capacity was very great, and a pumping machine was fitted to it to feed the other reservoirs in the temple[5].

50.2.1.en: He was concerned for the deliverance of his people from destruction, so he fortified the city so that it might withstand a siege [4].

50.3.0.en: 5 How glorious was he in the midst of the people, in his coming out of the house of the veil! 6 He was as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and as the moon at the full: 7 as the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High, 8 and as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds: and as the flower of roses in the spring of the year, as lilies by the rivers of waters, and as the branches of the frankincense tree in the time of summer: 9 as fire and incense in the censer, 10 and as a vessel of beaten gold set with all manner of precious stones: 11 and as a fair olive tree budding forth fruit, and as a cypress which groweth up to the clouds. When he put on the robe of honour, and was clothed with the perfection of glory, 12 when he went up to the holy altar, he made the garment of holiness honourable. 13 And when he took the portions out of the priests' hands, he himself stood by the hearth of the altar, compassed with a garland of his brethren round about, as a young cedar in Libanus; 14 and as palm trees compassed they him about. And all the sons of Aaron in their glory, 15 and the oblations of the Lord in their hands, before all the congregation of Israel. And finishing the service at the altar, that he might adorn the offering of the Most High Almighty, 16 he stretched out his hand to the cup, and poured of the blood of the grape. 17 He poured out at the foot of the altar a sweet-smelling savour unto the Most High King of all. 18 Then shouted the sons of Aaron, and sounded the silver trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard, for a remembrance before the Most High.

50.3.1.en: Sirach presents to us the person of Simon son of Onias as a wonderful model of a life of worship in holiness, whose features are the following: 1. The secret of his glory is that he meets with God in the Holy of Holies behind the house of the veil [5], and when he comes out he is surrounded by his people in great glory [5]. Thus Ben Sira ties together, in the life of the leader as a lofty model for every believer, a hidden life and a secret meeting with God as in the Holy of Holies, and that he not withdraw from the brethren. There is no contradiction between the glory that he enjoys secretly from God and the glory that shines from him through his love and service for his brethren [5]. 2. The secret of his holiness is that he rises above earthly things, and lives in the pledge of the heavenly things, like the morning star shining among the clouds, and like the moon in the perfection of its light when it becomes full [6]. 3. Wherever Simon son of Onias is found, glory, splendor, surpassing light and holiness do not leave him. Thus Ben Sira sees him in many situations that reveal various aspects of glory and splendor, of which we mention the following:

50.3.2.en: a. Behind the veil in the Holy of Holies [5] he enjoys solitude and a secret dialogue with the Holy One, and so is sanctified.

50.3.3.en: b. In the temple he is surrounded by his people in love for them; he serves them, teaches them and leads them in a spirit of love. How glorious he is! [5].

50.4.0.en: c. Among the clouds he shines like the morning star [6].

50.4.1.en: d. In the heaven he is like a moon perfect in splendor, in the state of a full moon, all light [6].

50.5.0.en: e. On high he is like a sun shining with the divine light upon the temple of the Most High [7].

50.5.1.en: f. In the divine presence he is like the rainbow, the sign of the divine covenant with men, shining in the clouds of the splendor of continual care [7].

50.6.0.en: g. In the fields he is like a flower among the roses, like a lily by a spring of water, or a cedar tree in the time of summer [8].

50.6.1.en: h. As he offers incense to God he himself becomes like fire, not to burn a man, but to burn fragrant incense, which points to the ascent of prayers to God.

50.7.0.en: i. As he uses the holy vessels he himself becomes a golden vessel, that is, a heavenly one for the service of the Heavenly One, set with precious stones [9].

50.8.0.en: j. In the garden of the house of the Lord he is like the fruitful olive tree, or like the cypress rising to the clouds [10].

50.9.0.en: k. As he puts on the garments of glory and goes up to the holy altar, the court of the house of the Lord is filled with the holiness that the Holy One pours out upon him [11].

50.9.1.en: l. When he takes from the hands of the priests the portions of the sacrifice, he sees the priests gathering round him in love, joy and exultation like a garland that encircles him.

50.9.2.en: m. As he poured the blood of the grape upon the altar, the Lord smelled it as a savour of good pleasure and delight on behalf of all the people.

50.9.3.en: n. As the sons of Aaron shout with exultation and praise and blow the trumpets of the word of God, this worship goes up before the throne of the Most High.

50.9.4.en: How glorious he was, surrounded by his people at his coming out from behind the house of the veil! [5].

50.9.5.en: This statement is probably a description of what the high priest does on the great Day of Atonement (Lev 16:23-25), when the high priest comes out of the Holy of Holies, from the veil, to the inner court. The Church has taken this rite for some feasts. Here he describes the service of the great Day of Atonement, revealing the skill of the high priest Simon son of Onias and the creativity in the service inside the temple. Ben Sira often records what he saw with his own eyes, as he records his feelings of joy and peace in his depths and in the hearts of those around him. He felt as though he had returned to the days of glory that Israel experienced at the completion of the building of Solomon's temple.

50.9.6.en: In verses 6-10 there comes a series of similes drawn from the beauty of nature, like those found in (Sir 24:13-17), to affirm the spiritual beauty of the high priest.

50.9.7.en: Like the morning star among the clouds, and like the moon at the full [6].

50.9.8.en: Or the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High, or the rainbow shining among the clouds of glory [7].

50.9.9.en: Or like the flower of roses in the days of the first fruits, or like the lily by a spring of water, or the branches of Lebanon in a summer day[6] [8].

50.9.10.en: Or like fire and incense in the censer, or a vessel of beaten gold set with every precious stone [9].

50.9.11.en: Or like an olive tree that bears fresh fruit, and like a cypress tree rising to the clouds [10].

50.9.12.en: v Let us then be like this, like olive trees, laden with commandments on every side. For it is not enough for us to become like olive trees; we must also be fruitful[7].

50.9.13.en: St. John Chrysostom: v Be like a green olive tree in the house of God. Never lose hope, but be fortified by faith with the flowers of sincerity, so that you may resemble that plant... indeed surpass it in bearing fruit, if every day you bring in a yield, overflowing with the giving of alms[8].

50.9.14.en: St. Basil the Great: In verses 11-13 he speaks of the morning and evening sacrifices which the high priest offers, which were mentioned before in (Sir 45:14), since the descendants of Aaron offered them twice every day without ceasing. The rites of this offering were known as tamid, that is, the continual offering (Ex 29:38-42). What is recorded in the Mishnah (Tamid 7:2-3) is that the ordinary priests stand around the high priest at the altar, presenting to him certain parts of the animal for the high priest to offer as a sacrifice. In this he resembles what students of the medical college and nurses do as they stand around the surgeon, handing him the special instruments so that he may perform the surgery.

50.9.15.en: When he put on the robe of glory, and was clothed with the perfection of honor, and as he went up to the holy altar, he made the court of the sanctuary glorious [11].

50.9.16.en: Moreover, the garment of Christ, or His clothing, points to the Church that clings to Him, for this garment the Lord washed with His pure blood... And as St. Cyprian says: [When the blood of the wine is indicated, what does it mean other than the wine of the cup of the Lord's blood?![9]] And St. Clement of Alexandria says: [The vine produces wine, and the Word offers blood; both bring health, the wine for the body and the blood for the spirit[10]]. And St. Augustine says: [What is this garment which he washes in wine, that is, washes in His blood from sin... but the Church[11].

50.10.0.en: And when he took the portion from the hands of the priests, standing by the hearth of the altar, a garland of brethren was around him, like a young cedar in Lebanon, and they surrounded him like the trunks of palm trees [12].

50.11.0.en: And all the sons of Aaron were in their glory, and the offering of the Lord was in their hands before all the congregation of Israel [13].

50.12.0.en: At the completion of the service at the altar and the ordering of the offering of the Most High Almighty [14], he would stretch out his hand to the cup, and pour out of the blood of the grape; he would pour it at the foot of the altar, a sweet-smelling savour before the Most High, the King of all [15].

50.12.1.en: Verses 14-15 describe the pouring out of wine [called libations, as mentioned in (Num 28:7-8)], which, as recorded in the Mishnah, was a daily rite accompanied by the blowing of the beaten trumpets.

50.12.2.en: v Now the blood of the Lord is twofold: one material, which saves us from corruption (1 Pet 1:8), and the other spiritual, by which we are anointed. To drink the blood of Christ is to partake of incorruption (Jn 6:55). But the Spirit is the power of the Word, in the same way as the blood is of the flesh. In the same way wine is mixed with water, and the Spirit with man. The first, the mixture, gives us joy so that faith increases, and the other, the spiritual, leads us to incorruption. The union of the two, that is, of the draught and the Word, is called the Eucharist, a gift worthy of praise, supremely splendid; those who partake of it are sanctified in body and soul, for this is the will of the Father. For man, a composite creature made by God, is united with the Spirit and the Word. In truth the Spirit is united entirely with the soul which depends on Him, and the flesh is united with the Word, since for its sake "the Word was made flesh" (Jn 1:14)[12].

50.12.3.en: St. Clement of Alexandria: As the Apostle Paul encourages his disciple to strive by the power of the Spirit for the preaching of the truth, fulfilling his ministry to the end with joy, he presented himself as an example, for he strove to the last breath. How wonderful indeed are his words: "For I am being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure is at hand" (2 Tim 4:6).

50.12.4.en: It is as though the Apostle had gone back in memory to Jacob, the father of all the tribes, who set up a pillar and poured a drink offering upon it and poured oil on it (Gen 35:14). This drink offering was probably of wine, which he offered on the pillar as the dedication of the first house to be set up for God in the history of salvation, as a reference to the gift of the joy of the Holy Spirit that fills the house of God, that is, His people. It is as though the Apostle saw, in the midst of his sufferings inside the prison as he went forth to the arena of martyrdom, that the spirit of divine joy fills the life of the Church through the sufferings of the Apostle.

50.12.5.en: And perhaps the Apostle, as he speaks of himself as a drink offering being poured out, remembers what the Law required, the offering of two lambs every day, the one in the morning and the other in the evening, while at its offering a drink offering of wine was made for it (Ex 29:40-41). It is as though the sacrifice of the Cross were tied to the joy of the Holy Spirit who is poured out upon the Church through the slain divine Lamb. This is our continual experience: in the liturgy of the Eucharist, as the Church offers to the Father, by the Holy Spirit, the offering of the only-begotten Son, His body given for us, He pours out upon her and within her His divine joy by the descent of His surpassing Holy Spirit! This is what has lifted the Church to sing the liturgy of the Eucharist as a hymn of surpassing joy, the work of the Holy Spirit, the giver of true joy!

50.13.0.en: Then the sons of Aaron would shout, and blow the beaten trumpets, and make a great sound as a remembrance before the Most High [16].

50.13.1.en: The sounds of the trumpets which the priests sounded were a proclamation of the beginning of the service or the sacrifice, and they were still in use in the age of Ben Sira (Num 10:2, 10); at that time all the believers would fall on their faces to the ground, and this moving spiritual atmosphere was interspersed with the praises of the Levites, while the people made supplication to the Lord.

50.13.2.en: "The Most High, the King of all": such a phrase was a hidden preparation for the salvation that the King of kings offers for the salvation of the whole world and not for the Jews alone.

50.13.3.en: v When our Lord Jesus comes (whose coming was symbolized of old by Joshua the son of Nun), He sends His priests, the Apostles, carrying trumpets of beaten (hammered) metal (Num 10:2; Ps 98:6), that is, the great heavenly teaching of preaching.

50.13.4.en: Matthew first sounded a priestly trumpet in his Gospel, and Mark and Luke and John also each blew his priestly trumpets. Peter also made his trumpet resound through his two epistles, as did James and Jude. John went on sounding his trumpet in his epistles, and so did Luke when he described the Acts of the Apostles. And finally there came the one who said: "I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last" (1 Cor 4:9); he sent forth thunderings with the trumpets of his fourteen epistles. He made the walls of Jericho, the idolatry that had been invented and the thoughts of the philosophers, collapse from their foundations[13].

50.14.s.en: 3. Exhortation to give glory to God

50.14.0.en: 19 And then all the people together hasted, and fell down to the earth upon their faces to worship their Lord God Almighty, the Most High. 20 The singers also sang praises with their voices, and in the great house was made sweet melody. 21 And the people besought the Lord, the Most High, by prayer before him that is merciful, till the solemnity of the Lord was ended, and they had finished his service.

50.14.1.en: At that time all the people would hasten together, and fall with their faces to the earth, to worship their Lord, the Almighty, the Most High [17].

50.14.2.en: The high priest alone was permitted to pronounce the holy name of God "Yahweh" when he announced God's forgiveness to the people (Lev 16:30). It is recorded in the Mishnah (Yoma 6:2): "When the priests and the people... hear the expression of the name (Yahweh) coming from the mouth of the high priest, they worship, and bow down, and fall on their faces."

50.14.3.en: And the singers also praised with their voices, and their songs were sweet with varied voices [18].

50.14.4.en: And the people also prayed to the Lord the Most High with a prayer before the Merciful, until the ordering of the Lord was finished and they completed His liturgy [19].

50.15.0.en: 22 Then he went down, and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Israel, to give the blessing of the Lord with his lips, and to glory in his name. 23 And he bowed himself down to worship the second time, that he might receive a blessing from the Most High.

50.15.1.en: Then he went down and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Israel, and gloried in His name (the name of the Lord) [20].

50.15.2.en: The service reaches its climax when the high priest stands to bless the people with the traditional priestly blessing found in (Lev 9:2; Num 6:24-26). As for pronouncing the name of the Lord "Yahweh," it was not permitted at that time for anyone to pronounce it, but it was replaced in reading by Adonai, except on the Day of Atonement, when the high priest was permitted to pronounce this fearful, blessed name to call down blessing upon the people.

50.15.3.en: Then they bow down to worship a second time, to receive the blessing from the Most High [21].

50.15.4.en: The Jews used to repeat the prostrations (metanoias), especially on the great Day of Atonement, which is what the Church does, especially on Great Friday, as she asks for God's mercies through the Cross as an atonement for our sins.

50.16.s.en: 5. A prayer for the peace of Israel

50.16.0.en: 24 And now bless ye the God of all, which only doeth wondrous things everywhere, which exalteth our days from the womb, and dealeth with us according to his mercy. 25 He grant us joyfulness of heart, and that peace may be in our days in Israel for ever: 26 that he would confirm his mercy with us, and deliver us at his time!

50.16.1.en: And now bless the God of all, who does great things in every manner, who glorifies our days from our birth, and deals with us according to His mercy [22].

50.16.2.en: May He grant us joy of heart, and may there be peace in our days, in Israel as in the days of old [23]

50.16.3.en: May He entrust to us His mercy, and may He redeem us in our days! [24]

50.16.4.en: "May He redeem us" or "save us": the Jews were awaiting the coming of the Messiah, the Savior! And this was fulfilled in the life, sufferings, crucifixion and resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ (Eph 1:7-14; Rom 8:22-23).

50.17.0.en: 27 There be two manner of nations which my heart abhorreth, and the third is no nation: 28 they that sit upon the mountain of Samaria, and they that dwell among the Philistines, and that foolish people that dwell in Sichem.

50.17.1.en: Two nations my soul abhors, and the third is no nation: [25]

50.17.2.en: Those who dwell on the mountain of Samaria[14], and the Philistines, and the foolish people who dwell in Shechem [26].

50.17.3.en: The Samaritans built a temple like the temple of Jerusalem on Mount Gerizim near Shechem, south of present-day Nablus, and the temple was still standing in the days of Ben Sira, although the Jews destroyed it in 128 B.C.

50.17.4.en: The present-day Samaritans still celebrate the Feast of the Passover beside their temple near Nablus. The Samaritans also claim that the line descending from Aaron the high priest has been broken, and that they alone, and no others, preserve an unbroken line descending from Aaron through Phinehas; this is what drove Ben Sira to hostility toward the Samaritans.

50.18.0.en: 29 Jesus the son of Sirach of Jerusalem hath written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, who out of his heart poured forth wisdom. 30 Blessed is he that shall be exercised in these things; and he that layeth them up in his heart shall become wise. 31 For if he do them, he shall be strong to all things: for the light of the Lord leadeth him.

50.18.1.en: This was added by the grandson, the translator of the book.

50.18.2.en: Jesus the son of Sirach the son of Eleazar of Jerusalem, who rained wisdom from his heart[15] in this book, I have written an instruction in understanding and knowledge [27].

50.18.3.en: Ben Sira signs his words, and encourages keeping and following them, for God gave them to him, and they are not from his own wisdom, or a merely human work, or something transmitted from the sages around him in the ancient world such as Hammurabi, Ahikar, Akhenaten and others; so he poured them out upon the sons of his people and withheld nothing.

50.18.4.en: Blessed is he who guides himself by them, for he who lays them up in his heart will be wise [28].

50.18.5.en: And if he does them, he will grow strong in everything, for the light of the Lord is his way [29].

50.18.6.en: What remains now is that they put them into practice, not merely passing them on in their gatherings, banquets and writings, and not treating them lightly either, for he who puts them into practice fulfills his hopes and is able to do all things, because the Lord will be a light to him through the words of wisdom that come out of the Law, also "Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path" (Ps 119:105).

50.19.s.en: May You shine with Your splendor upon Your Church!

50.19.0.en: v Grant us, O heavenly High Priest, to enjoy Your Holy Spirit, for He alone repairs Your temple in our hearts.

50.19.1.en: And He surrounds our souls like a wall of fire that protects us from the arrows of the enemy.

50.19.2.en: And He makes springs of living water burst forth within us.

50.19.3.en: v You raise up from our dark souls shining stars, and You send forth in us Your sweet fragrance, and You establish Your covenant within us, and fill us with Your peace.

50.19.4.en: You accept our prayers as a fragrant incense.

50.19.5.en: And You plant in us Your cross like an evergreen olive tree.

50.19.6.en: v Grant us Your righteousness as a garment in which we may be covered.

50.19.7.en: Set up Your altar within us, and Your Spirit will pour out heavenly joy.

50.19.8.en: We submit to You, and worship You rejoicing with the heavenly orders.

50.19.9.en: With pride the trumpets sound within us with Your life-giving word.

50.19.10.en: Turn our life into an unceasing hymn that we play all the days of our sojourn.

50.19.11.en: v You are our wondrous Redeemer.

50.19.12.en: The devil, with all his wiles and evil works, does not terrify us.

50.19.13.en: Through his wars, however fierce they become, we enjoy the crown of victory.

50.19.14.en: You are our support, our salvation, our glory and our crown.
